bull.b: Rapid growth in testing volume and revenue indicates broadening clinical adoption across Natera’s diagnostics platform. The raised 2026 revenue outlook further supports durable demand, while increasing scale can reinforce laboratory utilization and the company’s position with ordering clinicians.

Higher gross margins and a transition to sustained positive operating cash flow show that Natera is converting expanding scale into better economics. Although consistency still needs to be demonstrated, this foundation can support continued investment while reducing reliance on external capital.

Accelerating MRD utilization and new Medicare coverage strengthen Signatera’s clinical and commercial foundation. Repeated surveillance testing can support recurring demand, while published comparative evidence and broader coverage may improve adoption across indications and healthcare systems.

bear.b: Despite strong revenue growth and improved gross margins, Natera has not yet converted its platform into sustainable operating profitability. Continued losses limit the certainty of long-term earnings power and leave results dependent on maintaining growth while controlling operating expenses.

Natera is committing substantial resources to early cancer detection and other expansion initiatives before those programs produce revenue. This investment may create future opportunities, but it can pressure near-term margins and cash conversion if commercialization or regulatory progress takes longer than expected.

Because reimbursement materially affects test economics, uncertain MolDX decisions create a lasting execution risk for Natera’s growth plans. Delays or unfavorable outcomes could slow adoption, constrain realized pricing, and make the company’s expected margin expansion less dependable.
